title: A .gitignore for your exercise workspace
problem: Write the .gitignore for your workspace so Git ignores everything generated (virtual environments, Python caches, pytest caches, test reports) and never ignores your code or tests.
requirements: Ignore __pycache__/ directories and *.pyc files at any depth
Don't ignore .py files, tests or the .gitignore itself
contract: A file named .gitignore in this folder (one pattern per line; lines starting with # are comments)
expectedBehavior: In a repository using this .gitignore, `git check-ignore` reports .venv/lib/x.py and PY.M01.L03.E1/result.xml as ignored, and words.py as not ignored
edgeCases: Generated files in subfolders (each exercise has its own folder)
Your own source files must stay visible to git status
hints: Conceptual: a pattern without a slash in the middle matches at any depth. A trailing slash means 'directories only'.
Specific: you need about five lines: one each for the venv, Python caches (directory and file pattern), the pytest cache and result.xml.
Implementation: .venv/  __pycache__/  *.pyc  .pytest_cache/  result.xml, one per line. Check with `git check-ignore -v PATH`.
evaluation: No pattern that hides source files (e.g. *.py or *)
Readable: a comment per group is a plus
